clinician.final_diagnosis: Osteomyelitis of the clivus secondary to mucormycosis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 63-year-old male with previously known hyperglycemia and recent SARS-CoV-2 infection presented with weakness, fall, and right-sided facial droop. Initial CT showed advanced sinusitis. MRI/CTA revealed progressive sinusitis with abnormal gas in the skull base and clivus consistent with osteomyelitis. Fiberoptic nasal endoscopy showed invasive sinusitis. Histopathology from sinus/clival tissue biopsy demonstrated non-septate branching hyphae consistent with mucormycosis, confirming the diagnosis. Antifungal treatment with amphotericin B was initiated but changed to posaconazole due to pancytopenia. Repeat imaging showed worsening sinusitis despite treatment. Fungal culture results were not documented.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial CT demonstrated advanced sinusitis with right-sided facial droop and newly diagnosed diabetes mellitus
MRI/CTA showed progression of sinusitis with abnormal gas in the skull base and clivus indicating osteomyelitis
Fiberoptic nasal endoscopy demonstrated invasive sinusitis increasing suspicion for mucormycosis
Histopathology revealed non-septate branching hyphae consistent with mucormycosis from sinus/clival tissue biopsy
Antifungal treatment started with amphotericin B then switched to posaconazole due to pancytopenia; repeat imaging showed worsening sinusitis

remaining_uncertainties: Fungal culture microbiological confirmation is not documented
Detailed clinical outcome and follow-up beyond worsening sinusitis are not documented
